newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania workers protest against government policies.
newsitem.headline: Romania workers protest against government policies.

text.p: Around 3,000 construction workers protested in the streets of the Romanian capital on Thursday against looming unemployment and plant closures under government plans to restructure communist-era industries.
The protesters walked towards government's offices in central Bucharest, jeering and shouting "thieves, thieves" and shaking their fists.

The rally was called by the big Fratia (Brotherhood) trade unions federation, which claims up to one million members in construction and transport industries and in automobile and engine manufacturing.
"We want to remind the government of its promises to cut income and profit tax and to resume investments in construction," one protester said. Many had travelled to Bucharest from remote areas.
Thursday's rally was the latest in a series of labour protests over tough economic reforms launched by the centrists, who ousted ex-communists in elections last year.
The government has pledged radical surgery, including the closure of loss making industrial firms, to restore economic health and to gain new credits from international lending bodies.
The reforms have brought hardship, including higher prices and unemployment, to the already impoverished population.
Romanian average monthly pay is around $80. Official data shows that purchasing power has halved since the 1989 collapse of communism.
